newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Megawati says will not vote next week.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Megawati says will not vote next week.

text.p: Ousted Indonesian minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri said on Thursday she would not vote in general elections next week and told supporters not to cast their ballots for the party she previously led.
She appeared to stop short, however, of an illegal call for a total boycott of the five-yearly national and local elections next Thursday.
"With very deep concern, I declare today that I will not use my political right as a citizen (to vote) in this election," she told about 500 chanting supporters at her south Jakarta home.

Megawati, eldest daughter of Indonesia's late founding president Sukarno, was ousted by a government-backed faction as leader of the Christian-Nationalist Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) in June last year.
She has declared the takeover of the party illegal and has challenged it in the courts, so far without success.

"What is described as the PDI, it is the result of the Medan congress (when she was ousted last June). It is illegal and unconstitutional, therefore to vote for it on May 29, 1997, is also illegal and unconstitutional," she said.

The PDI, the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) and the ruling Golkar are the only parties legally entitled to contest the five-yearly elections for the House of Representatives next Thursday.
Golkar, in power for the last 30 years under President Suharto's rule, is expected to win the election comfortably.

The PDI, which campaigned on Indonesia's most populous island of Java on Thursday, has been badly hit by the split between Megawati supporters and the government-backed faction led by parliament's deputy speaker Surjadi. (Eds: one word)
The state-run electoral commission refused to recognise Megawati or any of her followers as candidates for the PDI in the election.
Addressing her supporters, Megawati wore a white dress -- the colour associated with "Golput", or the "white group" of people who show dissent by spoiling their ballots or not voting.
The mainly young audience at her home chanted "Long live Mega" and "Mega will win".
She said she had made her decision "after a one-sided elimination of my political rights as a citizen and as chairperson of the PDI..."

Political anaylsts have said the government wanted her ousted as PDI leader after her 1993 election to a five-year term over concern for her vote-drawing ability in the elections and a possible challenge to Suharto's re-election as president next year.

Witnesses said police in Bogor, a hill town near Jakarta, detained about 50 Megawati supporters when they tried to parade there on Thursday. There were no other reports of trouble during the day, a national holiday in Indonesia.
The three parties agreed before the election to campaign in different areas on different days to avoid confrontations.
The campaign winds up on Friday, with the PPP on the hustings in Java, where the bulk of election campaign violence has occurred between supporters of the PPP and Golkar.
PPP strongholds in south and east Jakarta were rocked last weekend and again on Tuesday in what political analysts said was the worst campaign violence since Suharto took power 30 years ago.
